findings.title: Codex never asks for approval
findings.rationale: `approval_policy = "never"` lets every command run without a human decision. Combined with `danger-full-access` (CX002) it is unattended arbitrary code execution.
findings.remediation: Use `on-request` or `on-failure`; reserve `never` for a disposable sandbox.

findings.title: Codex sandbox disabled (danger-full-access)
findings.rationale: `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` removes the filesystem and network sandbox; the agent can read any file and reach any host as the user.
findings.remediation: Use `workspace-write`; grant full access per task, not globally.

findings.title: Model provider reached over plaintext HTTP
findings.rationale: Prompts, code and credentials to `base_url`/`openai_base_url` travel unencrypted to a non-loopback host.

findings.title: Root-like path `/` marked trusted
findings.rationale: A `trusted` project skips the trust prompt and may auto-load that directory's instructions and MCP servers. Trusting `/` or the home directory trusts every repository; a very long trusted list suggests trust is granted reflexively.
findings.remediation: Remove the entry; trust individual project directories.

findings.title: Root-like path `/Users/me` marked trusted
findings.rationale: A `trusted` project skips the trust prompt and may auto-load that directory's instructions and MCP servers. Trusting `/` or the home directory trusts every repository; a very long trusted list suggests trust is granted reflexively.
findings.remediation: Remove the entry; trust individual project directories.

findings.title: Credential embedded in MCP server `search` (Google API key)
findings.rationale: Secrets in `env`, `args`, `headers` or the URL of a server are stored in plaintext and shared with every process that can read the file.
findings.remediation: Reference an environment variable (`${VAR}`) or a secret manager instead of the literal value.

findings.title: MCP server `search` runs unpinned package `mcp-server-search`
findings.rationale: `npx -y pkg`, `pkg@latest` or `uvx pkg` resolves and executes whatever the registry serves at launch time. A compromised or typosquatted release runs with your privileges on next start.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version (e.g. `mcp-server-search@X.Y.Z`) or install once and point `command` at the binary.

findings.title: Codex workspace-write sandbox allows network access
findings.rationale: `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` removes the filesystem and network sandbox; the agent can read any file and reach any host as the user.
findings.remediation: Disable unless the task needs egress; network lets exfiltrated data leave.

findings.title: Codex hook on `TurnEnded` has no recorded trusted hash
findings.rationale: Hooks run on lifecycle events with the user's privileges and belong to the trust boundary. Codex records a trusted hash per hook; a hook without one has not been approved.
findings.remediation: Review the script; Codex will prompt to trust it on next run.

findings.title: Model provider is a loopback HTTP proxy
findings.rationale: Prompts, code and credentials to `base_url`/`openai_base_url` travel unencrypted to a non-loopback host.
findings.remediation: Confirm the proxy itself uses TLS upstream and is not reachable from other hosts.

findings.title: Codex hook executes a shell command
findings.rationale: Hooks run on lifecycle events with the user's privileges and belong to the trust boundary. Codex records a trusted hash per hook; a hook without one has not been approved.
findings.remediation: Approved (trusted hash recorded). Re-review if the script changes.
